newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrians may cast protest vote in first EU poll.
newsitem.headline: Austrians may cast protest vote in first EU poll.

text.p: Austrians vote on Sunday in their first European parliamentary elections, with the far right hoping to pick up protest votes from a people angry at welfare cuts, job losses and tax increases.
Pollsters said almost half of the electorate was still undecided and two-thirds of the waverers were considering delivering a rap on the knuckles to Chancellor Franz Vranitzky's Social Democrats.
One poll said 57 percent of Austrians, pointing to a wave of bankruptcies, takeovers and job losses, believed that 21 months in the European Union had brought them more ills than benefits.
"The politicians knew this would happen. They should have told us at the start," said a middle-aged Viennese woman who had yet to decide how, or if, she would vote.

Far-right leader Joerg Haider hopes to unsettle the ruling coalition of Social Democrats and conservative People's Party by winning at least a quarter of the national vote, compared with 22 percent in general elections last December.
Haider's brand of nationalism and anti-immigrant invective has gone down well with voters worried about unemployment and a perceived increase in crime.
He has accused the coalition parties of bungling Austria's entry into the European Union and has demanded the renegotiation of payments to Brussels.
The Social Democrats have seen their support slump to around 31 percent, one of the lowest levels since World War Two and down from 38 percent last December.
The People's Party has held steady at around 28 percent, helped by the personal appeal of its leading EU candidate Ursula Stenzel, an Austrian television personality.

The polls open for the 5.8 million voters at 7 a.m. (0500 GMT). Computer projections are expected at 6 p.m. (1600 GMT) when the last polling stations close and first unofficial results are likely to be announced around 9 p.m. (1900 GMT).

Full official results on who will occupy Austria's 21 seats in the European Union parliament in Strasbourg will be issued later in the week but they are unlikely to diverge substantially from the preliminary count.
Vienna's 1.1 million people also vote on Sunday in state elections that look certain to end half a century of Social Democrat rule in the capital and could open the door to the far right.
The People's Party is also braced for a disappointment in Vienna, where its support has dropped to 15 percent from 18 percent last time round.
